blocking_findings.scenario: The contract says record accepts each measured envelope using fixtures from the real runs, and the review context blocks on missing real-run evidence for any of the three runtimes. The real-run fixture test only covers codex-verdict.json and claude-envelope.json, and tests/IntentSystem.Cli.Tests/Fixtures/G834/ has no cursor fixture. The cursor path is tested only against a hand-built envelope, `new { type = "result", subtype = "success", is_error = false, result = <bare JSON>, session_id = "s" }` (lines 553 and 1213). The cursor parser in src/IntentSystem.Cli/Commands/CrossRuntimeReviewVerdict.cs:150 runs `JsonDocument.Parse(result.Trim())` on the envelope's `result` text, and cursor-agent has no `--json-schema` flag. If a real cursor run wraps the verdict in a ```json fence or adds any prose, or its envelope keys differ from the guessed shape, every cursor verdict is refused with `cross-runtime-review-verdict-invalid`. A team with a cursor conductor, or a cursor cross-runtime reviewer, could then never satisfy the gate. Nothing at this head shows the pinned cursor invocation was run or that its output shape was measured.

notes: I checked that HEAD is 5e83fb53dc97acb71a6db762ba65e8f3446784ee and reviewed the diff 9e461d8f..HEAD. The base named in the contract is main. PR #90834 does not resolve on GitHub (`gh pr view` returns 'Could not resolve'), so I could not check the pasted real-run evidence, the pr-transition base-vs-head diff, the full-suite counts, or exact-head CI from the PR body.

In a scratch copy of the head, focused tests (G834, AutomationPrTransition, GuideSoloConductor, Ledger filters) ran in Release: 158 passed, 0 failed. I did not run the full suite. `git diff --check 9e461d8f HEAD` is clean.

No launch: the new CrossRuntimeReview*.cs files and ReviewCrossRuntimeCommand.cs contain no Process, ProcessStartInfo or shell execution. The only new external call is the read-only `gh pr view --json headRefOid` in GhCliGitHubLabelMutator.ReadPullRequestHeadSha. It runs only for `approved` of a declared team in a gated repo.

Undeclared teams and ungated repos are unchanged by inspection. The gate block is guarded by `transition == approved && IsGatedRepo(repo)`. An undeclared team returns (null, null). The new result field uses WhenWritingNull, and the text line is written only when the field is non-null. The tests compare against a host with no declaration on the same build, not against the base build.

Gate: records on other heads never count (IsHead). A block from a runtime clears only through that runtime's later record on H, or, for rereview, through its latest record on an earlier head being approve. Unreadable records (bad JSON, failed validation, raw sha256 mismatch) make the decision `blocked`. Refusals return before the label write and CI-wait clearing in both write and dry-run.

Records use FileMode.CreateNew for the raw copy and the record, check existence first, and are covered by a collision test. Both head checks are present: the echoed head_sha in record, and the current PR head in pr-transition.
The pinned invocations match the contract's allow-list text. None contains write-enabling flags (`--permission-mode plan`, `-s read-only`, `--mode plan --sandbox enabled`).

The emitted schema leaves out the `$schema` draft 2020-12 keyword because Claude Code 2.1.269 rejects it (per the code comment). The contract says draft 2020-12, so the PR should state this deviation with the measured error.

The claude-envelope.json fixture is a probe run with placeholder head 0123456789abcdef... and notes ['probe'], not a run against this unit's PR head. The envelope shape is measured, but the AC asks for runs against the unit's own PR head, recorded in a scratch host.

The ledger row says 'An intent-cli without G834 ignores the table.' Confirm that pre-G834 CliConfigLoader tolerates an unknown top-level `cross_runtime_review` table; otherwise that compatibility claim is wrong.

Minor: the record reader only catches IOException, UnauthorizedAccessException and InvalidOperationException. Any other exception from a malformed record (for example from TOML or JSON edge cases) would crash status or pr-transition instead of reporting `record-unreadable`. It still fails closed.
